| [CASE-052](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-052.md) | Stokely Carmichael's two speaking styles, kept apart by audience and collapsed by broadcast | As boyd (2008) reports it after Meyrowitz (1985: 43): the civil rights leader Stokely Carmichael used very different rhetorical styles with black and with white audiences. | [CASE-053](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-053.md) | Contextuality tests on human meaning and judgement data: a held null, and positive results that miss pragmatic content or power | The published tests of contextuality proper on elicited human judgements, read together. The null that meets every condition is the record's own [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md): attitudinal and lexical data, none contextual under Contextuality-by-Default. Wang's thesis adds a Bell-type null on meaning judgements. The positive results miss a condition: Cervantes and Dzhafarov's "Snow Queen" is contextual with high reliability but its content is instructed attribute matching, and Lo, Sadrzadeh and Mansfield's Winograd schemas have the right content but a violation of about one standard deviation. No contextual pragmatic data are documented; "none in behavioural data" is too broad. | Active |
| [CASE-054](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-054.md) | Joking relationships: one kind among the Crow and in Africa with no route between them, descended between Crow and Hidatsa, and a transported tale beside them | Radcliffe-Brown defined the joking relationship as one comparative kind and placed the Crow joking-relative and Dogon and Thonga joking in it; no historical route joins the Crow to West or South-East Africa. | [CASE-057](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-057.md) | Swapping the two persons of a dyad: nonreciprocal T/V address is changed by the swap and reciprocal address is not, with a constructed French–English dyad and a three-person teasing round | Built on a documented distinction. Two constructions extend it. A master-and-servant dyad in French and in modern English is changed by the swap in one realization and fixed by it in the other. A three-person teasing round gives a group whose automorphism can swap characters, so the anchoring of [CLAIM-249](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-249.md) has work to do. | Active |
| [CASE-058](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-058.md) | FactBank's source-relative factuality labels and Kiesling et al.'s stance-triangle annotation: one stance construct annotated reliably, the interpersonal ones not | FactBank labels one event's factuality separately for each source that reports it, so a proposition held fixed gets different commitment labels by source, and trained annotators agree at κ = 0.82. | [CASE-059](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-059.md) | Tatiana's letter in Eugene Onegin III: вы to ты and back, lost in Kline and half kept in Spalding | Tatiana's letter to Onegin opens with the formal вы, breaks into the intimate ты at "я твоя", and returns to вы in its last lines; only the pronouns mark the moves. | [CASE-065](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-065.md) | Two satisfaction questions in German and in a back-translated Chinese version: an order effect that reverses across a rendering, with the Clinton–Gore poll as the scale of the 2ε bound | Haberstroh, Oyserman, Schwarz, Kühnen and Ji (2002), Experiment 2, asked German and Chinese students the same two satisfaction questions, in a back-translated Chinese version, in both orders. The part–whole correlation depends on order in the German administration and reverses in the Chinese one, and the authors explain it by a pragmatic mechanism. Only correlations are reported, so the case shows the bound's contrapositive in kind, not in number. Moore's Clinton–Gore poll, held through [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md), supplies the number: an order effect of total variation about 0.095, against a sampling floor of about 0.03 per order at poll sizes, so 2ε is about as large as the effect it would certify. | Active |
| [CASE-066](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-066.md) | Dolly's slip into ты in Anna Karenina I.4, and three English translations that carry it three ways | In Anna Karenina I.4 Dolly says one sentence to Stiva with ты amid вы, and the narrator says so. The later two add words not in the Russian to carry the relation. Tolstoy himself says вы and its dictionary equivalent vous differ in coldness. A documented instance of the compensation mechanism; the evidence on what readers recover is translators' and the author's, not readers'. | Active |

| [CASE-072](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-072.md) | Hafez's "Shirazi Turk" in English: one ungendered beloved rendered as a maid, as God and as a boy | The opening of Hafez's ghazal 3 names a beloved, "that Shirazi Turk", whose sex and nature the Persian leaves open. A documented instance of the half of a change of cover in which the rendering decides what the source left open. The disagreement on the source is among translators and scholars; no reader agreement has been measured. | Active |
